beginner.stem: How many protons does a Magnesium atom have? (That number is also its place on the table.)
beginner.explanation: Magnesium is element 12. A neutral atom has 12 protons and 12 electrons.

beginner.stem: Which element has the symbol Mg?

beginner.stem: Who does this catalog credit for finding Magnesium?

beginner.stem: Which history line belongs to Magnesium?
options: Magnesia, a white earth from Magnesia in Greece, was long confused with lime.
Carl Gustaf Mosander, a student of Berzelius, separated a new earth from cerium nitrate in 1839.
Sulfur, called brimstone, was known from volcanic deposits and from metal ores long before it was classed as an element.
Robert Bunsen and Gustav Kirchhoff, using the spectroscope they had just developed, saw deep red lines in the mineral lepidolite in 1861.
beginner.explanation: Magnesia, a white earth from Magnesia in Greece, was long confused with lime.

beginner.stem: How does the catalog describe the discovery of Magnesium?
options: Robert Bunsen and Gustav Kirchhoff examined the mineral lepidolite with the spectroscope they had just built.
Joseph Black had already shown that magnesia alba was not lime.
Carl Gustaf Mosander suspected that ceria was not a single earth.
Sulfur was gathered from volcanic ground and from the roasting of sulfide ores long before it had a place in a list of elements.
beginner.explanation: Joseph Black had already shown that magnesia alba was not lime.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Magnesium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: A district in Greece gave its name to a white earth that physicians and chemists kept confusing with lime. Joseph Black insisted the two earths were not the same.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Magnesium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: Humphry Davy recognized the metal and coaxed out only a little of it. A generation later another chemist prepared enough that the element could be studied in bulk.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Magnesium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: A spring in England tasted bitter and drew visitors who hoped the water would heal them. The dissolved salt was a magnesium compound, not a mystery of the well.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Magnesium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: Burning magnesium throws a white light strong enough to freeze a face in a dark room. Photographers and signalers adopted the flame before factories thought about weapons.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Magnesium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: The same white flame that lit a photograph could be turned to destruction. Wartime records include magnesium as an incendiary metal, a fact of history rather than a set of instructions.

beginner.stem: One listed emission line of Magnesium is near which wavelength?
beginner.explanation: The catalog lists a Magnesium line at 383.23 nm (violet).

beginner.stem: What color name does the catalog give the 383.23 nm line of Magnesium?
beginner.explanation: That Magnesium line is labelled violet.

beginner.stem: Which of these sits in the same column as Magnesium?
beginner.explanation: Beryllium shares group 2 with Magnesium.
